minutes.headline: Select Board continued a liquor license transfer hearing two weeks and heard an update on the 2023 tax assessment investigation.
minutes.summary: Public comment and a long question period centered on the FY2023 property assessment investigation, the town manager's role on it, open meeting law, and abatements. The board appointed a member to the architectural preservation commission and continued a package store license transfer hearing to February 21. It also approved prior minutes, heard a town manager report including FY23 budget pressures, and adjourned.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether repeal and replace of the abatement process could be considered if the investigation finds wrongdoing.
Objected to the town manager sitting on the investigation subcommittee as a conflict of interest, and urged the subcommittee to comply with open meeting law.
Asked about number of lakefront homes, abatements, who new assessors report to, and whether the principal assessor model should be reconsidered.
Said the land was over-assessed, not the houses, and questioned the point of assessors visiting.
Asked whether the investigation covers why non-lakefront valuations rose little.
Asked whether the investigation will examine the judgment ('art') part of assessment.
Asked when it was known and who knew about the assessment increases, and whether land characteristics will be assessed.
Cautioned against comparing lakes and assuming lakefront is more valuable.
Asked whether a Proposition 2 1/2 override occurred and suggested assessments are a back door to raise revenue.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 4-0 to appoint a member to the architectural preservation district commission for a term ending June 30, 2023.
After the first motion was not audible, the board continued the package store license transfer hearing to February 21 at 7:15 PM once the applicant agreed.
Most of the meeting was a status update and public questions on the FY2023 property assessment investigation, including the town manager's role and abatements.
The board decided to keep a placeholder on the annual town meeting warrant to override the APDC denial; the warrant closes March 20.
The town manager reported a projected health insurance deficit and a snow and ice overrun, with transfers and pavement management funds named as cover.

why_it_matters: The assessment investigation bears on how property values, and so tax bills and abatement requests, were set for FY2023, and residents asked whether the process itself should change.
Covering the health insurance and snow and ice overruns by transfers and by pavement management funds can mean less money for other uses, and transfers are normally voted at town meeting.
The APDC override placeholder is an article residents may be asked to vote on at annual town meeting.
watch_next: February 21: the continued package store license hearing at 7:15 PM, plus an ARPA and investigation update.
February 28: senior tax relief presentation; the town meeting warrant closes March 20.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the Lockwood appointment, the budget figures, the snow and ice overrun, both transfer discussions and the School Committee liaison. Differences otherwise come from caption misspellings of names and from items one record has and the other lacks. The one substantive difference is that our minutes record a continuance vote on the package store license hearing to Feb 21 and the official minutes record no such vote.
